ip_top_stories.title: Another judge agrees: AI-Created art isn't copyrightable
ip_top_stories.summary: A second federal judge has ruled that art generated solely by AI cannot be protected by copyright, reinforcing the emerging judicial consensus that copyright requires human authorship. The decision adds further weight to the legal principle established in earlier rulings on AI-generated works.

ip_top_stories.title: China Issues Draft Regulations on AI Copyright Infringement
ip_top_stories.summary: China has released draft regulations addressing copyright infringement in the context of AI-generated content, signalling a significant regulatory move in one of the world's largest AI markets. The draft rules are expected to shape how AI companies handle training data and generated outputs under Chinese law.

ip_top_stories.title: Delhi HC directs decision on copyright plea for AI-created artistic work
ip_top_stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed India's Copyright Office to decide within eight weeks whether an AI-generated artwork can be registered under Indian copyright law, in a case brought by a US researcher. The ruling is being closely watched for its potential implications for global AI intellectual property frameworks.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic's Legal Overhang: Piracy Trial Could Unravel Ethical AI Premium
ip_top_stories.summary: Analysis of the upcoming Anthropic copyright trial suggests the outcome could significantly undermine the company's positioning as an ethically responsible AI developer. The case centres on allegations that Anthropic trained its models on pirated books, with potential consequences for its commercial valuation and the broader AI industry.

ip_top_stories.title: Cox v. Sony Music Comes to Hollywood
ip_top_stories.summary: The Cox v. Sony Music copyright liability case, in which an internet service provider was found liable for contributory infringement by its subscribers, is drawing attention for its potential application to Hollywood content distribution. The case raises questions about platform and intermediary liability in an era of AI-assisted content creation and distribution.

ip_further_links.title: Tech's AI Coding Boom On Collision Course With Copyright
ip_further_links.summary: The rapid expansion of AI coding tools is raising significant unresolved copyright questions about the use of open-source and proprietary code in AI training datasets.

ip_further_links.title: AI Code Leak Exposes the Fault Lines of Copyright
ip_further_links.summary: A leaked AI codebase has highlighted deep unresolved tensions around copyright ownership of AI-generated and AI-assisted code.

ip_further_links.title: [Courting Controversy] Now You See Me, Now You Don't: The Illusion of Authorship
ip_further_links.summary: Legal commentary examining the contested nature of AI authorship and the philosophical and legal challenges in attributing creative ownership to machine-generated works.

ip_further_links.title: AI And Human Authorship Requirement: Reflections From The US Position And Implications For Indian Copyright Law
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of how the US copyright requirement for human authorship is influencing the developing Indian legal position on AI-generated works.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI Freezes UK Stargate Project: Energy Costs and Copyright Rules Delay 8,000-GPU Plan
ip_further_links.summary: OpenAI has paused its UK Stargate data centre project, with copyright regulatory uncertainty cited alongside energy costs as a key factor in the delay.

ip_further_links.title: Apple accused of copyright infringement over AI training on YouTube videos
ip_further_links.summary: Apple is facing allegations that it used YouTube video content without authorisation to train its AI systems, adding to the growing number of copyright infringement claims against major tech companies.

ip_further_links.title: Fordham 33 (Report 2): Top 5 Takeaways: Data Governance, Privacy, & Cybersecurity in an AI World
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat's report from the Fordham IP Conference covers key discussions on data governance, privacy, and cybersecurity as they intersect with AI development and intellectual property law.

ip_further_links.title: Cox v Sony: Infringers gonna infringe – unless service providers encourage them
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat analysis of the Cox v Sony ruling examines the standard for secondary copyright liability for internet service providers whose subscribers engage in infringement.

ip_further_links.title: India AI Copyright Case: Delhi Court Review Impacts Global IP Value
ip_further_links.summary: Commentary on how the Delhi High Court's review of AI copyright eligibility in India could have ripple effects on global intellectual property valuation and AI investment.

ip_further_links.title: AI-Generated Animation: Implement Legal Regulations to Protect Copyright Holders
ip_further_links.summary: Commentary calling for clearer legal regulations to protect copyright holders from the growing use of AI in animation and creative content production.
